title: Bahá’í (Badí‘) calendar dates, 1 to 1157 B.E.
dates: Each Gregorian date is the day on which the Bahá’í day ends. A Bahá’í day begins at sunset, so it begins on the evening before the date given.

confidence.label: convention
confidence.note: Before 172 B.E. there was no single calendar: these dates follow the Western convention set out under Shoghi Effendi (Naw-Rúz on 21 March). See docs/calendar-rules.md for how practice in the East differed.

confidence.label: published
confidence.note: Matches the dates published by the Bahá’í World Centre for 172 to 221 B.E.

confidence.label: cross-checked
confidence.note: Computed; agrees with the independent badiDate library (JPL ephemeris) for every year to 2351.

confidence.label: estimate
confidence.note: Computed; the uncertainty in the Earth's rotation (Delta T) means some years may be a day out where the equinox falls close to sunset in Tehran.
